findings.text: Shared completion helper for emulated guest operations. An error input is converted into a guest visible protection fault, while success advances past the current instruction and signals continuation to the caller.

Generic handler for guest translation invalidation requests. It loads a two element operand from guest address space, checks identifier range and enablement consistency plus address canonicality, and either faults the guest or performs a targeted invalidation or requests a wider flush.

Top level hypercall dispatch for the virtual CPU. Xen handling is preferred when enabled for the virtual machine, followed by Hyper-V handling when enabled for the virtual CPU, with remaining cases delegated to a generic path that receives privilege level and a completion routine.

SVM exit entry for control register moves. Decode assistance and a validity signal in exit information are required, with fallback to generic emulation when absent. Direction and register selection are derived from the exit code, including a dedicated selective write code that maps to the zero register.

Selective write filtering for the zero control register is active only during nested execution when the parent enables the selective control. Masked bits are excluded from comparison between current and proposed values, and a surviving difference raises a selective exit that nested handling may claim.

Supported control register traffic is bounded. Writes cover zero three four and eight, reads cover zero two three four and eight, each routed to the matching architecture accessor with directional tracing of register and value.

Malformed control register traffic is contained. Missing validity, missing decode assistance, and unsupported register numbers do not affect the host; they divert to generic emulation or raise a guest undefined opcode fault that is reported as handled.

Trap entry for control register writes that carry the new value directly in exit information. Zero four and eight are accepted with architecture notification after zero and four updates, while other indices produce a guest undefined opcode fault.

Debug register exit entry with distinct modes. Protected encrypted guests return immediately without changes, guests with no active debugging clear intercepts and request a reload before reentry, and remaining guests require decode assistance before delegating to generic debug helpers with standard completion.

Priority level write handling builds on control register interception. With an in kernel interrupt controller the result completes locally, while with a userspace controller a decrease in level is reported to userspace as a priority change request instead of completing in kernel.

Extended feature register trapping sanitizes the trapped value by removing the virtualization enable bit before calling common register handling, preventing validation failures for guests without the corresponding CPU feature, followed by standard fault or advance completion.

Encrypted guests with protected state face narrow register access. Most intercepted accesses are blocked with zeroed data or an error depending on protected state support, a single unintercepted exception plus explicitly unintercepted indices remain allowed, and host initiated accesses bypass guest capability checks.

SVM register serving prefers hypervisor maintained copies and control block fields, with feature derived values for selected configuration registers. Unknown indices and shared configuration cases fall through to the common layer, and capability gated registers reject guest access without the matching guest feature.

Page attribute handling separates nested guest view from host view when nested paging uses an independent guest table. Guest originated accesses observe the current control block copy, host originated accesses observe the primary copy, allowing save and restore operations to be ordered arbitrarily.

Virtualization control register updates enforce lock semantics. Reserved bits are rejected, the lock and disable bits become immutable once disable is set, and a disable request is rejected while the extended feature enable bit remains set.

Branch record virtualization depends on host support. Without support reads return zero and writes are ignored or reported unsupported, with support the four last branch and exception address registers map to distinct save area slots and guest writes are rejected while host restores are accepted.

Translation invalidation families have distinct contracts. Single address and single context forms validate enablement and canonicality before invalidating, all context forms request a guest wide flush without distinguishing global scope, unknown types fault, and prediction state handling is left to the flush path.

Pause exit entry expands the adaptive spin window and reports spinning to the scheduler. Encrypted guests are always treated as user context because privilege level is unavailable, other guests distinguish kernel versus user spinning by current privilege before skipping the instruction.

SVM entry for translation invalidation requires the guest feature and a canonical operand address. Missing feature raises an undefined opcode fault, malformed address raises a protection fault, otherwise type and address extracted from exit information are forwarded to the generic handler.

Bus lock exits leave the kernel with a flag plus a recorded instruction pointer and a completion callback. If userspace returns with an unchanged pointer the hypervisor arms a one step bypass via a counter, otherwise execution resumes at the updated location, with nested state remembering the last event.

Hypercall instruction exits during nested execution fault unless the request qualifies as a nested flush assist handled by the hypervisor. Non nested exits and qualifying assists enter generic hypercall emulation.

Register emulation completion for encrypted guests diverges on error. Instead of normal fault injection it delivers a protection fault through the hypervisor communication block exception mechanism, while success follows the standard advance path.

Auxiliary timestamp register updates that go through the user return facility execute with preemption disabled across slot update, preventing migration between slot programming and caching of the new value.

Exit and register state flows through control and save areas. Control provides exit code and information words plus a bus lock counter, save provides segment bases syscall targets speculation controls debug controls branch records and CET related fields, with explicit dirty marking for CET and branch groups on change.
Validity for control register intercept information is carried in the top bit of the first exit information word.
Control register tracing encodes direction with a leading flag alongside register number and value, using zero for reads and one for writes.
